summary.en: Communal clashes in South Sudan have intensified, with 16 dead and 34 injured in recent fighting and dozens feared missing after an attack on Jonglei’s Miny Island, while 27,000 people are displaced in Upper Nile amid escalating Kitgwang fighting. The UN envoy is urging South Sudanese leaders to choose consensus over confrontation, and the African Union has expressed deep concerns over the renewed clashes, while Uganda has defended its military deployment in the country. A pastor received death threats in a refugee camp and a Juba Dal activist was hacked to death in Cumilla, reflecting targeted violence against civilians. The EU and Germany-funded SGBV prevention project has concluded after four years. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
